fixes.explanation: Right, false. Wisdom says she was "…rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men." (Proverbs 8:31) She says she delights in them. That's the opposite of keeping her distance.

Yes, friend. Wisdom takes her stand "…at the crossroads…" (Proverbs 8:2). She also cries out "…the gates to the city…" (Proverbs 8:3). Crossroads and city gates, out in the open. That's a woman who wants to be heard.
The temple never comes up in this passage. Wisdom is out by the road, at the crossroads and beside the city gates (Proverbs 8:2-3). No front desk, no appointment. She cries out in public places.

Funny thing, she's the one raising her voice. She "raises her voice" (Proverbs 8:1). What she asks of the simple ones and fools is to learn to be shrewd and to gain understanding (Proverbs 8:5). Nothing here tells them to hush.

That's what she says: "To fear the LORD is to hate evil…" (Proverbs 8:13) She goes on to name some of what she hates, like evil conduct and perverse speech. So fearing the LORD isn't only a feeling. It comes with hating evil.
Wisdom stands at the crossroads and city gates (Proverbs 8:2-3). She never ties fearing the LORD to staying away from anybody. She says, "To fear the LORD is to hate evil…" (Proverbs 8:13)

Good guess, friend, but priests don't appear in these verses. Wisdom says, "By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws…" (Proverbs 8:15) The blank is kings, the ones wearing the crowns. Rulers come right after them.

True. Wisdom says, "I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me." (Proverbs 8:17) Notice that it's a promise for those who seek her early. Those are the ones who will find her.
Nice try, friend, but changing it isn't mentioned. Wisdom says, "Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it." (Proverbs 8:33) Nobody's asked to edit the instruction. The word is ignore.
Hiding it sounds sneaky, but it isn't in this verse. She says, "Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it." (Proverbs 8:33) Ignoring it is the warning, not hiding it.

Law is a good-sounding word, friend, but it isn't in this verse. It says, "For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD." (Proverbs 8:35) The blank is favor, and it comes right after life.
